# 2 Chronicles Chapter 12 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** After Rehoboam's position as king was established and he had become powerful, he abandoned the law of the LORD — and all Israel followed him.

**2** In Rehoboam's fifth year, because they had been unfaithful to the LORD, King Shishak of Egypt attacked Jerusalem.

**3** He came with twelve hundred chariots, sixty thousand horsemen, and an innumerable horde from Egypt — Libyans, Sukkites, and Cushites.

**4** He captured the fortified cities of Judah and advanced as far as Jerusalem.

**5** The prophet Shemaiah came to Rehoboam and the leaders of Judah who had gathered in Jerusalem because of Shishak, and told them, "This is what the LORD says: 'You have abandoned Me, so I am abandoning you to Shishak.'"

**6** The leaders of Israel and the king humbled themselves and said, "The LORD is just."

**7** When the LORD saw that they humbled themselves, He spoke to Shemaiah: "They have humbled themselves. I will not destroy them. I will soon give them deliverance, and My wrath will not be poured out on Jerusalem through Shishak.

**8** But they will become his subjects, so they will learn the difference between serving Me and serving earthly kingdoms."

**9** So Shishak king of Egypt attacked Jerusalem and carried off the treasures of the LORD's temple and the royal palace. He took everything, including the gold shields Solomon had made.

**10** King Rehoboam replaced them with bronze shields and assigned them to the commanders of the guard who protected the entrance to the royal palace.

**11** Whenever the king went to the LORD's temple, the guards came carrying the shields, then afterward returned them to the guardroom.

**12** Because Rehoboam humbled himself, the LORD's anger turned from him, and He did not destroy him completely. Indeed, there was still some good in Judah.

**13** King Rehoboam established himself firmly in Jerusalem and continued to rule. He was forty-one when he became king and reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city the LORD had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel to put His name. His mother was Naamah, an Ammonite.

**14** He did evil because he never really set his heart on seeking the LORD.

**15** The events of Rehoboam's reign, from beginning to end, are recorded in the chronicles of the prophet Shemaiah and of the seer Iddo. There were continual wars between Rehoboam and Jeroboam.

**16** Rehoboam rested with his ancestors and was buried in the City of David. His son Abijah succeeded him as king.


---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **12:1**: "When he became powerful, he abandoned the LORD" — this is the Chronicler's thesis statement for nearly every failed king. Power reveals character, and Rehoboam's character is shallow.

- **12:8**: "They'll learn the difference between serving Me and serving earthly kingdoms" — God turns judgment into a lesson. You want to know what life without Me looks like? You're about to find out.

- **12:10**: Gold shields replaced with bronze — the most potent symbol of decline in the entire book. Solomon's glory, reduced to cheap imitations paraded around on ceremonial occasions. The form survives; the substance is gone.


— PNEUMA
